cases.description: A well-formed, witness-signed response with in-scope, agent-signed events and valid Merkle proofs verifies.
A response under the vendor-neutral network.ink namespace, witness-signed over its actual type, verifies (ink/0.4 dual-accept).
A response signed under the legacy namespace but relabelled to network.ink fails the witness envelope signature.
A fresh witness response with tree size 0, no events or proofs, and the empty-tree root verifies.
A protocol other than ink/0.1 is rejected.
A type other than the audit-query response type is rejected.
An empty messageId is rejected.
A rootHash that is not 64 lowercase hex is rejected.
A tree size of 0 with non-empty events is a fabricated state and is rejected.
A proof leafIndex not less than treeSize is rejected.
A response whose messageId does not match the one the verifier asked about is rejected.
A response signed for a different requester is rejected (prevents cross-requester replay).
A response from an unexpected witness DID is rejected when the verifier pins serviceDid.
Changing rootHash after signing breaks the witness envelope signature.
A valid response checked against a different witness key is rejected.
An event whose messageId differs from the envelope is out of scope and is rejected.
An event in scope by messageId but whose agentId and counterpartyId both exclude the requester is rejected at the scope step.
A response with more events than proofs is rejected.
A duplicate event id is rejected.
Two proofs for the same eventId are rejected.
A proof referencing an eventId not present in events is rejected.
A proof whose sibling is replaced does not reconstruct rootHash and is rejected.
An event whose agentSignature is by a different key fails the required per-event provenance check, even though the witness envelope and Merkle proofs are valid.
An event whose agentId has no resolvable key fails the per-event provenance check.
A later checkpoint with a larger tree is consistent with the response.
A later checkpoint with a smaller tree means the witness rewound the log and is rejected.
A later checkpoint at the same size with a different root is a fork and is rejected.
